name: Eastern Lowland Kenyah
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Smith, Alexander D. 2017. The Languages of Borneo: A Comprehensive Classification. PhD thesis, U. Hawai'i at Manoa (covers Kenyah varieties

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 2013. The Austronesian Languages (revised edition). Canberra: Asia-Pacific Linguistics. Sec. 4.1.3, p. 186.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Areal remark only: 'many of the languages of coastal Sarawak, and some interior languages have final stress in citation forms, but penultimate stress in phrasal context'; Kenyah not named.

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 2017. The Lowland Kenyah posterior implosives. Language and Linguistics 18(2): 177-200. DOI 10.1075/lali.18.2.01blu.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only for Long Sela'an/Long Ikang Lebu' Vu' and Long San (WESTERN Lowland Kenyah, long1406): Appendix fn. 11, p. 198: 'Stress was invariably recorded as final in citation forms.' Eastern Lowland varieties appear only in fn. 2 p. 182 (Long Dunin = Uma' Pawa', close relative of Lebu' Kulit, left unclassified) and fn. 9 p. 192 (Lebu' Kulit cluster reflexes); no stress statement for them.

sources.citation: Smith, Alexander D. 2017. The Languages of Borneo: A comprehensive classification. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. (Kenyah sec. 2.11.4 pp. 252-256 with primary data for Lebo' Kulit of Sungai Asap and Uma' Pawe of Long Apu; sec. 3.2.1.1.1(.1) pp. 264-266; tree p. 441)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing for any Kenyah variety. Eastern Lowland Kenyah is treated only for nasal-stop cluster retention, *-a > -e raising, *z > s and Kayan loans; the dissertation's stress remarks concern Merap, Segai-Modang, Hliboi Bidayuh and West Kalimantan Malayic only.

sources.citation: Soriente, Antonia. 2013. Undergoer voice in Borneo: Penan, Punan, Kenyah and Kayan languages. NUSA 54: 175-203; Soriente 2013. Variation in aspect and modality in some languages of Northeastern Borneo. NUSA 55: 193-218; Soriente 2014. Studying linguistic and cultural contact in Borneo. Antropologia 1(1): 59-81; Soriente 2018. Deixis in Borneo: Kenyah and Punan. Ethnorêma 14.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: All four treat Lebu' Kulit (Long Tungu data) morphosyntax, deixis, TAM or classification; 'stress' occurs only in the non-phonological sense. Silent on word stress.

sources.citation: Soriente, Antonia. 2008. The classification of Kenyah languages: a preliminary statement. In W. Khanittanan & P. Sidwell (eds), SEALS XIV vol. 2: Papers from the 14th meeting of the Southeast Asian Linguistics Society (2004), 49-62. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics E-5.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Classification/ethnonym paper; lists 12 Kayan-Kenyah sound changes (incl. lowering of high vowels in the penultimate syllable) but no statement on accent placement.

sources.citation: Soriente, Antonia (ed.). 2006. Mencalèny & Usung Bayung Marang: a collection of Kenyah stories in the Òma Lóngh and Lebu' Kulit languages. Jakarta: Atma Jaya University Press. Front matter pp. i-xliv incl. Introduction and 'Notes about the Orthography' (Lebu' Kulit consonant/vowel charts pp. xlii-xliii). Part 1 of the MPI Jakarta web edition.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Gives Lebu' Kulit segment inventory and orthography only; no mention of stress/accent anywhere in the introduction or orthography notes (book has no grammar sketch; remainder is texts and glossaries).

sources.citation: Revel-Macdonald, Nicole. 1982. Synchronical description at the phonetic and syllabic level of Modang (Kalimantan Timur) in contrast to Kenyah, Kayan, and Palawan (Philippines). In A. Halim, L. Carrington & S.A. Wurm (eds), Papers from the Third International Conference on Austronesian Linguistics, vol. 2, 321-331. Pacific Linguistics C-75. DOI 10.15144/PL-C75.321.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Stress statement only for Modang (p. 324, fixed final accentuation). Kenyah data include Kc = 'Lepo' Kulit' of Long Noran (an Eastern Lowland Kenyah village) but Kenyah is discussed only for post-schwa gemination (p. 329); no Kenyah stress statement.
